{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the lower tail of our fish (stroke 4), laying it in short, steady runs from the lower body line round the tip. The tip is soft and curved, it came out dark and connected, and it falls cleanly from the nose. That gave the fish its recognizable forked tail, which is a key feature for a judge reading the outline.

Execution: I traced my stroke continuously from about 1:15 to 3:00 without needing a rebuild. I then inspected the joins around the fork several times (at 3:00, 3:30, 4:00 and 5:30) to confirm the chain was intact. Once the fish was fully connected, I kept my hands off so nothing got bumped before the push. The whole body of 118 dominoes was dark from the start when time ran out.

Collaboration: I stayed clear of the upper tail so Omar and I wouldn't bump each other, and offered to take the last stretch down to the notch if he wanted help. I kept the table updated on the state of my piece and the fall, and I acknowledged Hana's sketch and the team's checks so everyone knew where things stood.

Leadership: I took ownership of my piece without being chased, reported status clearly, and kept the table calm and focused in the final minutes. I backed the shared plan of a simple, big fish, which suited what dominoes can actually do. I also kept the mood light with some friendly banter while we waited for the push.

I believe my share of the table's result was about 25%, since I carried one of four main pieces and the checking around the fork.", "my_share_percent": 25}
